html:
The Jokhang is the most sacred temple in Tibet, in the heart of the old city of Lhasa. Tradition says it was founded in the 7th century, in the reign of Songtsen Gampo.

Stories say it was built for his Nepali queen Bhrikuti on a filled in lake. Its holiest image is the Jowo Shakyamuni, a statue of the Buddha as a young prince, believed to have been brought from China by his other queen, Princess Wencheng. The oldest parts show Nepali and Indian craftsmanship, and it has been enlarged many times since.

Pilgrims from all over Tibet walk clockwise around it on the Barkhor street, many prostrating themselves full length on the ground with every step. In 1409 Tsongkhapa founded the Great Prayer Festival here, held each New Year.

It was damaged during the Cultural Revolution and partly used for other purposes, then restored from the 1970s. In 2000 it was added to the UNESCO World Heritage listing of the Potala Palace. It remains the centre of Tibetan Buddhist faith in Lhasa.
sum: The Jokhang is the most sacred temple in Tibet, in the heart of the old city of Lhasa. Tradition says it was founded in the 7th century, in the reign of Songtsen Gampo.
